**It can be a good option—but it’s a projector screen, not an electronic back-seat display.** It clips into the Model Y and can be set up for rear-seat, tailgate, or panoramic-roof viewing; the screen is about 47–50 inches. You’ll need a compatible portable projector, and it’s intended for viewing **while parked**, not while driving. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

The key caveat is fit: Aurzen says it’s designed for the **2025–2026 Model Y Refresh**; fit may vary on earlier Model Ys. So I’d consider it if you have the refreshed model and want a removable movie setup, but not if you want a plug-and-play screen for passengers to use on the road.

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s official U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99**. Aurzen lists free shipping, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty; the product is U.S.-only.
